description: The worked examples in Krippendorff's step-by-step guide to computing alpha: binary, nominal with two observers, and four observers with missing values under four metrics.

source.title: Computing Krippendorff's Alpha-Reliability
source.journal: Departmental Papers (ASC), Annenberg School for Communication, University of Pennsylvania
source.table: Example A (p. 2 to 3), example B (p. 3 to 4), example C reliability data matrix and coincidence matrix (p. 4), nominal alpha (p. 5), ordinal, interval and ratio alphas (p. 8)

notes: Every number was transcribed from the PDF above. Data are kept as printed: one row per observer, one column per unit, null where the paper prints a dot for a missing value.
Example C is the paper's 4 observers by 12 units matrix; section D reuses it for the ordinal, interval and ratio metrics.
coincidences.asPrinted keeps the paper's notation: fractions as text and a dot for an empty cell.

A.section: A. Binary or dichotomous data, two observers, no missing data

B.section: B. Nominal data, two observers, no missing data

C.section: C. Nominal data, any number of observers, missing data; D. Any metric, any number of observers, missing data
